query_snapshot: For hydrogen chloride, which barriers does the archived NIOSH table place in its 8-hour and 4-hour groups, and what additional hazard language appears in the entry?
final_answer:
Evidence-grounded answer:

- The archived NIOSH protective-clothing table places hydrogen chloride in the 8-hour barrier group: Butyl, Responder, and Tychem. [NIOSH/Chemical Protective Clothing Page/INDEX A: https://www.newenv.com/NIOSH/RCPC.htm]
- The archived NIOSH protective-clothing table places hydrogen chloride in the 4-hour barrier group: Teflon and PE/EVAL. [NIOSH/Chemical Protective Clothing Page/INDEX A: https://www.newenv.com/NIOSH/RCPC.htm]
- The archived NIOSH table entry for hydrogen chloride includes the additional hazard language / recommendation: “Prevent skin contact.” [NIOSH/Chemical Protective Clothing Page/INDEX A: https://www.newenv.com/NIOSH/RCPC.htm]
